question: A person who spends 33% of his monthly income is able to save ₹6,298 per month. His monthly expenses (in ₹) are:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Saving % = 100% − 33% = 67%

Given, 67% = ₹6,298

Expenses (33%) = (6,298 ÷ 67) × 33

Expenses = 94 × 33 = ₹3,102

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,102.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30e909c340caf8d70187b0f0457d9c0c87eac6a97700a9a7ccf28813619b66cd.png] 

**Given:**

Monthly **Expenses** percentage = 33%

Monthly **Savings** = ₹6,298

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenses + Savings

**Calculations:**

⇒ Savings % = 100% − 33% = 67%

⇒ 67% of Income = ₹6,298

⇒ 1% of Income = 6,298 ÷ 67

⇒ 1% of Income = 94

⇒ Monthly Expenses (33%) = 33 × 94

⇒ Monthly Expenses = ₹3,102

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,102.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage change is calculated as (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100.

Income-Expenditure Relation

Income is always considered the base (100%) when calculating percentage savings or expenditure unless stated otherwise.

Successive Percentage

If income increases by x% and then y%, the net change is [x + y + (xy ÷ 100)]%.
